comparisons.note: At 2.0% support, both algorithms discover identical 492 itemsets. Apriori executes quickly because candidate pairs are few (492).
FP-Growth completed 1.75x faster while consuming ~95x less memory (~98 MB vs 9.35 GB peak RAM). Mathematically identical itemsets (2,743) empirically verified.
Apriori timed out after 120s due to combinatorial candidate explosion (>1.3M candidate pairs and triples), confirming CA1 theoretical claims.

conclusion: Empirical evaluation confirms that where both algorithms terminate, Apriori and FP-Growth yield mathematically identical frequent itemsets. However, FP-Growth demonstrates dramatic computational and memory efficiency, maintaining sub-100MB footprint at 1.0% support while Apriori experiences severe combinatorial candidate explosion consuming 9.35 GB of RAM, and completely timing out at 0.5% support.
